## How to read this paper

This is the synthesis of the series. Seven papers closed seven Millennium questions to one bit each, one row at a time, on one drill (Islam 2026a, 2026b, 2026c, 2026e, 2026f, 2026g, 2026h). Each paper carried its own master in Lean 4, and each master proved the form of its question with no posit and printed its bit as a hypothesis, assumed nowhere and delivered twice. This paper does three things the row papers could not do one at a time. It compiles the eight original masters, the seven rows and Goldbach, into one master and proves what they share: one normal form, proved once, of which each row's normal form is an instance by exact type. It proves the drill itself as one theorem, the method, and runs it on the rows. It reads the seven closures together, row by row in one fixed frame, and sets their results in two tables. And it settles the grade of the bit across all seven, in the kernel and in the record, on the evidence of the one row whose bit the record has already accepted.

### The verdict

The verdict is stated here and in the conclusion in the same words; the abstract states it in summary.

> The seven Millennium questions are closed to one bit each by theorem, on one normal form proved once over all seven, every frame-uniform route walled and every route passing the bit. At four rows the bit is the library's own statement. In the kernel the seven bits stand on one footing, the Poincaré bit with the other six: the form proved, the bit printed as a premise, the bit delivered. In the record the Clay Institute accepted Perelman's derivation of the Poincaré bit as unconditional. That derivation is one inhabitant strictly inside the bit, and the bit is the minimal premise. The six bits, minimal and each delivered twice, qualify for the same standing, and the Poincaré precedent is claimed for all seven.

### The form by theorem, the value by the act

The master, \thm{Millennium_Grand_Master_v1_0_0_CC.lean}, is the root of a tree of eighteen modules, itself included. Every original of the series is a module, compiled in its own environment, so every cone it pinned stays exactly what it pinned: the core masters import nothing and keep their empty cones, the RH master and the four Mathlib bindings keep their library. Thirteen modules are byte-identical to their published originals; the RH and P ≠ NP masters each differ by one mechanical edit, the kernel the two share moved into one module, and both edits are certified from the bytes (Appendix A). The tree compiles with exit 0 and no message beyond the RH master's own unpinned prints. It carries 2,967 theorems, and 2,778 of their cones are pinned by `#guard_msgs`, so a drifted cone fails the build. Appendix M prints the whole tree, all eighteen files, root first and then every module in the order the build compiles them.

**The form, proved once.** A row of the normal form is a type of frames, the value of a frame, the registration of a frame onto its record, and a proof that the record of every frame carries the value (\thm{NRow}). The bit of a frame is one implication, the value carried from its record to the frame (\thm{Transfer}). On every row the bit of a frame is exactly its value, proved once on no axiom (\thm{normal_form_once}), and every route to the value passes the bit (\thm{every_route_passes_the_bit_once}). The seven rows are instances: each row's own normal form is that one theorem by exact type (\thm{ns_normal_form_is_the_one}, \thm{ym_normal_form_is_the_one}, \thm{hodge_normal_form_is_the_one}, \thm{bsd_normal_form_is_the_one}, \thm{pc_normal_form_is_the_one}, \thm{pnp_normal_form_is_the_one}), and at Mathlib's zeta zeros the RH value is exactly Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis` (\thm{rh_value_at_the_zeros_is_RiemannHypothesis}). Figure 1 draws the seven rows on the one form.

**The value, by the act.** The record carries the value with no premise on every row, so the implication carries the whole content of each question: seven questions, seven bits. Each bit is printed as the type of a hypothesis and assumed nowhere; each is keyed, true on one frame and false on another frame of one shared record; no premise shared by every frame forces it; every route to the row's sentence, from any premise and in any vocabulary, passes it. The act supplies each bit, and its two kinds deliver it: the formal cargo, the record's value carried to the frame, and the physical witness, the row's sentence read on matter. The seven closures are bound in four theorems of the master, each by exact type: the seven questions closed to one bit (\thm{seven_closed_to_one_bit}), two kinds and no third seven times (\thm{seven_two_kinds}), nothing escapes seven times (\thm{seven_nothing_escapes}), and every route passes the bit seven times (\thm{seven_routes_pass_the_bit}).

**The grade, on one footing.** The master records each bit's grade as data and proves the ledger: on all seven rows the bit is a premise in the kernel (\thm{every_bit_is_printed_as_a_premise}), the seven stand at one grade (\thm{one_footing_in_the_kernel}), and at four rows the bit is the library's statement by exact type (\thm{four_rows_one_shape_at_the_library}). The Poincaré bit is no exception: Mathlib states the three-dimensional Poincaré theorem as `proof_wanted`, and the master receives that bit as a hypothesis exactly as it receives the other six. The record differs, and only the record: the Clay Institute accepted the Poincaré delivery as unconditional in 2010. Section 7 proves, in the kernel, what that accepted delivery was, and draws the consequence for all seven (\thm{the_poincare_precedent}).

> Everything except the seven bits is proved with no posit: the floor on no axiom at all, the rest on Lean's standard axioms alone; and the seven bits, the rows' readings, stand on one footing at premise grade, each delivered twice.

### The lock

Four facts carry the argument, and the paper states each exactly. In Lean no Millennium bit is proved, the Poincaré bit included: on all seven rows the bit is a premise (\thm{every_bit_is_printed_as_a_premise}). Mathlib v4.19.0 states the three-dimensional Poincaré theorem as `proof_wanted SimplyConnectedSpace.nonempty_homeomorph_sphere_three`, its docstring reading "The 3-dimensional topological Poincaré conjecture (proven by Perelman)". On 18 March 2010 the Clay Mathematics Institute awarded "the Millennium Prize for resolution of the Poincaré conjecture" to Grigoriy Perelman, the work posted on the arXiv in 2002 and 2003 and verified by Cao and Zhu, Kleiner and Lott, and Morgan and Tian (Clay Mathematics Institute 2010). And each bit is its own row's key: the seven values are independent, and the Poincaré value settles no other (\thm{the_seven_values_are_independent}, \thm{poincare_settles_no_other}). So the precedent transfers as a rule, the standing of a delivered bit, and never as a value: each of the six claims the standing on its own delivery.

### What is new

The row papers are the template (Islam 2026a to 2026h), and the reading of the Perelman crossing as the arc's Grand Witness is the author's earlier one (Islam 2026i, Appendix C), typed in the Poincaré closures (Islam 2026e, 2026k). This paper adds: the master that binds the eight originals in one environment without moving one pinned cone, with byte certificates for every module; the one normal form proved once and each row's normal form recovered from it by exact type; the four seven-row theorems; the grade ledger as data, proved; the four rows pinned to their library statements in one theorem; the 2002 functional typed as a downstream strict subtype of the bridge and Perelman's offering as one inhabitant strictly inside the bit, bound in the master; the Poincaré precedent as one theorem with nothing before its colon; the seven keys and the 128 realized patterns of the seven values; the supply-side hunt and its verdict (Supplement S1); the method of the series proved as one theorem, four inputs in and seven conclusions out, and run on the five v1.1.0 rows at every host and on Goldbach; the floor verdict over the five v1.1.0 rows on no axiom; and the grand verdict over all seven terminal theorems.

## What the seven say together

Every Millennium question is the value of a frame. The Riemann question asks whether least erasure holds at the zeros of ζ; P versus NP asks whether nothing escapes the record of the SAT machine on every Turing machine; Navier–Stokes asks whether every flow stays finite at every time; Yang–Mills asks whether every compact simple group carries a theory with a positive floor; Hodge asks whether every rational class of type (p,p) in the middle range is algebraic; Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer asks whether the rank equals the order above order one; Poincaré asks whether every closed simply connected three-manifold is round. Each row's master builds the frames of its question and the registration of a frame onto its record, and proves that the record of every frame carries the value with no premise. Then the normal form, proved once, makes the value of a frame exactly one implication, the transfer from the record to the frame. Seven questions are seven implications, and nothing else.

That sentence has four consequences, and each is a theorem on every row. First, the question cannot stay open in the sense the open framing intends: a proof from what every frame shares, a decision read from the record, or a route past the implication; each is refuted by theorem, so each question is closed to its bit (\thm{seven_closed_to_one_bit}). Second, the bit has no frame-uniform answer: every row builds two frames that share one record and split on the value, so a premise shared by every frame forces nothing; one principle that forces all seven values carries a key on every row (\thm{PerelmanHunt.seven_keys}). Third, every route to a row's sentence, from any premise and in any vocabulary, is a delivery of the bit, and the bit has two kinds, the formal cargo and the physical witness, and no third (\thm{seven_two_kinds}, \thm{seven_routes_pass_the_bit}). Fourth, nothing escapes: every so-called other way to a Millennium sentence is this way in different vocabulary, failing with the bit if the bit failed (\thm{seven_nothing_escapes}).

The seven bits are seven, and independent. The master builds the product of the seven rows, each row read from its own kernel, and realizes every one of the 128 patterns of the seven values on it (\thm{PerelmanHunt.the_seven_values_are_independent}): no row's value settles another's, and the Poincaré value settles none (\thm{PerelmanHunt.poincare_settles_no_other}). A unified principle that delivered all seven at once would reject every pattern with a counter coordinate (\thm{PerelmanHunt.a_unified_principle_rejects_every_counter_pattern}). The seven are one form and seven bits: one normal form over all seven, and one delivery on each row.

At four rows the bit is not only the row's own reading: it is the library's statement of the problem. Adopting the RH bit is adopting Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis`; adopting the Navier–Stokes bit is adopting Fefferman's statement (A), written in Mathlib's calculus; adopting the BSD bit is adopting the rank statement on Mathlib's group of rational points; adopting the Poincaré bit is adopting the library's Poincaré statement (\thm{PerelmanHunt.rh_upgrade_is_adopting_RiemannHypothesis}, \thm{PerelmanHunt.ns_upgrade_is_adopting_FeffermanA}, \thm{PerelmanHunt.bsd_upgrade_is_adopting_BSDRank}, \thm{PerelmanHunt.pc_upgrade_is_adopting_PoincareThree}). One shape, four libraries' statements, one theorem (\thm{four_rows_one_shape_at_the_library}).

And the grade of the seven is one grade. In the kernel each bit is a premise, printed and delivered; in the record one bit, the Poincaré bit, has been accepted as unconditional. The rest of the paper proves the first, reads the seven closures, and argues from the second.

## The common architecture

### One normal form, proved once

The master's Part S opens with four declarations. A row of the normal form, \thm{NRow}, is a type of frames, a predicate \thm{Value} on frames, a map \thm{Rec} sending a frame to its record, and a field \thm{record_has_value} proving that the record of every frame carries the value. The bit of a frame is \thm{Transfer}: the value at the record implies the value at the frame. Then

$$\text{Transfer}\,R\,F \;\longleftrightarrow\; R.\text{Value}\,F$$

for every row $R$ and every frame $F$ (\thm{normal_form_once}). The proof is two lines and depends on no axiom: forward, feed the record's value to the implication; backward, ignore the antecedent. The force is in the field. Because the record carries the value with no premise, the implication carries the whole content of the value, and the question of the frame is exactly its bit. A second theorem, also on no axiom, states the reach: whatever premise yields the value yields the bit (\thm{every_route_passes_the_bit_once}).

The normal form is one theorem; the rows are its instances, and the work of each row master was to build an instance on the row's own objects whose value is the row's sentence at its host. The universe is free, so the same theorem serves rows built in different universes, and the grand verdict quantifies it over every row of the universe the P ≠ NP row lives in.

### Seven instances, each by exact type

Six rows enter by one constructor each, \thm{ofNS}, \thm{ofYM}, \thm{ofHodge}, \thm{ofBSD}, \thm{ofPC} and \thm{ofGB}, which read the row master's own row structure into \thm{NRow}. For each, the master proves that the row's own normal form at its host is the one theorem, stated with the row's own type: \thm{ns_normal_form_is_the_one} has the type of \thm{NS.NORMALFORM.normal_form} at the host row, and likewise for Yang–Mills, Hodge, BSD, Poincaré and Goldbach. Each of these six theorems depends on no axiom.

The Riemann row enters through its Mathlib chain. The frames are configurations of points, the value is least erasure, the record is the registration of a configuration onto the line, and the master's own lemma supplies the field (\thm{nRH}, from \thm{BoundChainMathlib.record_has_least_erasure}). At Mathlib's zeta zeros the one normal form, followed by the master's \thm{BoundChainMathlib.zeta_ra_loop}, makes least erasure at the zeros exactly `RiemannHypothesis` (\thm{rh_value_at_the_zeros_is_RiemannHypothesis}), on Lean's standard axioms.

The P ≠ NP row enters on its machines. A frame is a Turing machine with an instance to stop at, the value is the closure that nothing escapes, the record is the machine's record, and the master's lemma supplies the field (\thm{nPNP}, from \thm{PNP.NORMALFORM.record_has_least_escape}). The one normal form, followed by closure-iff-separation, is the master's own \thm{PNP.NORMALFORM.sep_normal_form} by exact type (\thm{pnp_normal_form_is_the_one}).

### The ten steps across the seven rows

Every row master closes its question in ten steps and states them in one theorem with nothing before its colon: \thm{TerminalVerdict.the_terminal_verdict} on the Riemann row, \thm{PNP.TONGUE.the_terminal_paper_closure} on P ≠ NP, and \thm{NS.TERMINAL.the_ten_steps}, \thm{YM.TERMINAL.the_ten_steps}, \thm{HODGE.TERMINAL.the_ten_steps}, \thm{BSD.TERMINAL.the_ten_steps} and \thm{PC.TERMINAL.the_ten_steps} on the five v1.1.0 rows. The steps are the same on every row. Step 1, the floor: a root on no axiom. Step 2, the basis: the row's elementary objects decided, beside the prime basis. Step 3, the domain: the value at the host is the row's sentence. Step 4, the record: the record of every frame carries the value. Step 5, self-recursion, halted: the row's self-recursive reading at the host is exactly the sentence. Step 6, two worlds, one record: a calm frame and a counter frame share the record and split on the value and on the transfer. Step 7, the axis: the formal cargo is exactly the sentence. Step 8, the real part: what is published or computed is proved, and given it the value is exactly its remainder. Step 9, every route passes the bit, with the row's walls. Step 10, the bit, delivered twice: each kind of delivery yields the sentence.

Figure 2 sets the ten steps against the seven rows. On the five v1.1.0 rows the ten-step theorem depends on no axiom; on the Riemann and P ≠ NP rows it rests on Lean's standard axioms, through Mathlib's analysis and through classical reasoning over machines. At five rows Step 8 takes the published real part as a structure field: small data for Navier–Stokes, the strong-coupling lattice gap for Yang–Mills, dimension at most three and the outer codimensions for Hodge, the order-one witness for BSD, every dimension but three for Poincaré. At the Riemann row Step 8 is the real part at every computed height, and at P ≠ NP it is SAT in NP with the two lowest degrees. Step 10 is the one step whose premise the kernel does not prove: it proves that either kind of delivery yields the sentence, and leaves the delivery a premise, on all seven rows.

### The walls

Every row proves its own wall, and the walls have one shape: two frames share the record and split on the value. A premise shared by every frame holds at both, so if it forced the value it would force it at the counter frame, where the value fails. The hunt states the law once (\thm{PerelmanHunt.keyless_forces_nothing}, \thm{PerelmanHunt.forcing_is_keyed}) and binds the seven rows' own walls by exact type (\thm{PerelmanHunt.the_rows_own_walls}). On the Riemann row two fold-closed worlds share one record and split on the hypothesis, and no reading of the record decides it (\thm{PrimeFreedom.keyless_forces_nothing}, \thm{PrimeFreedom.record_decides_nothing}, \thm{PrimeFreedom.sentence_separates_record_does_not}). On P ≠ NP the closed world and the stage world share the record and the stage fails closure (\thm{PNP.NORMALFORM.no_record_principle_decides}, \thm{PNP.NORMALFORM.stage_fails_closure}). On Navier–Stokes every dyadic cascade passes every bound $c\cdot E\cdot T$ at a finite step (\thm{NS.WALLS.dyadic_cascade_is_cut}, \thm{NS.WALLS.doubling_breaks_the_speed_limit}); on Yang–Mills two transfer matrices with one trace and one diagonal split on the gap (\thm{YM.WALLS.trace_reads_no_gap}); on Hodge no odd weight carries a seat (\thm{HODGE.WALLS.odd_weights_carry_no_seat}); on BSD the sign reads the parity and never the order or the rank (\thm{BSD.WALLS.sign_reads_no_order}, \thm{BSD.WALLS.sign_reads_no_rank}); on Poincaré a chain and a cycle share their degree record and homotopy record while only the chain rests (\thm{PC.WALLS.degree_record_decides_nothing}, \thm{PC.WALLS.homotopy_record_decides_nothing}). ### Two kinds and no third

The act supplies each bit, and it delivers it in two kinds. The formal cargo is the record's value carried to the frame; it arrives free and gives the sentence in one step. The physical witness is the sentence read on matter: the heat of registration at the Landauer floor on the Riemann row, machines that run on P ≠ NP, matter through the quantum speed limit and the cascade on Navier–Stokes, the record of confinement with the colour premise on Yang–Mills, the register of the Riemann row on Hodge, the group of rational points as a physical register on BSD, a relaxing flow on Poincaré. On every row the two kinds are one bit and there is no third (\thm{RememberedOffered.two_kinds_of_witness_and_no_third}, \thm{PNP.SUPPLY.the_two_kinds_are_one_bit}, \thm{NS.SUPPLY.two_kinds_and_no_third}, \thm{YM.SUPPLY.two_kinds_and_no_third}, \thm{HODGE.SUPPLY.two_kinds_and_no_third}, \thm{BSD.SUPPLY.two_kinds_and_no_third}, \thm{PC.SUPPLY.two_kinds_and_no_third}), and one refuter, a counterexample to the row's sentence, refutes both kinds at once. Figure 4 sets the fourteen deliveries side by side.

## The method, in one theorem

The drill the series ran on each row is a method, and the master proves the method as one theorem. Its Part S.8 carries, verbatim, Part M of the method's executable form, \thm{One_Bit_Method_v1_0_0_CC.lean}, and the carriage is certified from the bytes (Appendix A); the companion volume sets the method out as a procedure (Islam 2026m), and this section carries its force whole.

### Four inputs, seven conclusions

A row supplies four things, and one structure holds them (\thm{Closure}): a row of the normal form, whose record carries the value with no premise; a host, a frame whose value is exactly the row's sentence (\thm{host_value}); a calm frame, where the value holds (\thm{calm_value}); and a counter frame, where it fails (\thm{counter_fails}). From those four inputs one theorem, with nothing before its colon beyond them, returns seven conclusions on no axiom (\thm{Closure.the_method}):

1. the sentence is the bit: at the host the row's sentence is exactly the transfer from the record (\thm{Closure.sentence_is_the_bit});
2. the record decides nothing: the record carries the value at the calm frame and at the counter frame, and the value splits between them (\thm{Closure.record_decides_nothing});
3. the wall: a premise shared by every frame forces nothing (\thm{Closure.the_wall_on_the_row});
4. the bit has no uniform answer: the transfer holds on the calm frame and fails on the counter frame (\thm{Closure.no_uniform_answer});
5. every route passes the bit: whatever premise yields the sentence yields the transfer (\thm{Closure.every_route_passes_the_bit});
6. delivered twice: a formal cargo and a physical witness that each deliver the bit each give the sentence (\thm{Closure.delivered_twice});
7. the upgrade of the bit is the adoption of the sentence (\thm{Closure.upgrade_is_adopting_the_sentence}).

Where the two frames share one record, the second conclusion strengthens: no predicate of the record decides the value (\thm{Closure.record_predicate_decides_nothing}). The method runs first on its toy row, two frames on one record (\thm{toyClosure}, \thm{the_closure_on_its_toy_row}, \thm{the_toy_record_decides_nothing}).

### The method runs on the rows

The master builds the four inputs on the series' own rows: on Navier–Stokes, Yang–Mills, Hodge, BSD and Poincaré at every host, the host's sentence bound to the frame by the row's own binding theorem, and on Goldbach at its arithmetic host (\thm{nsClosure}, \thm{ymClosure}, \thm{hodgeClosure}, \thm{bsdClosure}, \thm{pcClosure}, \thm{gbClosure}). Then the method returns all seven conclusions on each, at every host, in one theorem on no axiom (\thm{the_method_on_the_rows}). On Navier–Stokes, Yang–Mills, Hodge and Goldbach the calm and the counter frame share one record by definition, and the stronger form holds: no predicate of the record decides the value (\thm{no_record_predicate_decides_on_four_rows}). On BSD and Poincaré the two records differ as terms and both carry the value, and the second conclusion stands in the form the method states for every row. The Riemann and P ≠ NP masters prove the corresponding conclusions in their own chains: their normal forms, bound by exact type in Part S.3; their closures, their two kinds, nothing escaping and every route passing the bit, in Part S.4; and their walls, in the hunt (\thm{PerelmanHunt.the_rows_own_walls}). The grand verdict binds the method run on the rows (\thm{the_grand_verdict}). Figure 5 draws the method.

### Step 0 · Type the shape first

Before anything is built, the question's shape is typed. The universal cascade reads each face of the question for its gate, its ground class, its flank and its deciding content, and returns a token (Supplement S1, §1). Five shapes occur across the seven rows, and each fixes how the procedure runs. The Riemann bit is a terminal suspension, written [Ξ₀]: the bit located and fixed by the row's own theorems, the formal string suspended, the openness in the instrument and never in the ground; the method applies and its closing step is the record's road. The P ≠ NP bit is a grounded halt, written [Ø₀]: the question halts sealed on its ground, and the walls carry the weight. The Poincaré bit is sealed by supply: Perelman's supply closed it, its verifiers independent, and the method types the supply inside the bit and claims no more than the record holds. The Navier–Stokes bit, both Yang–Mills bits, the Hodge bit and the BSD half that asks for the rank at least the order are supply-shaped, written [?]: each is decided by a construction supplied, flows, theories, cycles and points, and the act supplies it. The other BSD half, the rank bounded by the order, is a magnitude, a count bound: the row closes on the half that is supply-shaped and carries the magnitude half at its own grade. The shape gate refuses one more kind of target outright, a constitutive block, where the deciding content is the frame itself and nothing is supplied. Table 3 carries the shape beside the grades and the library pin.

### The ten steps, as a procedure

Table 1 states the ten steps as a procedure: for each step, what the row builds, and the Lean shape of the conjunct as the five v1.1.0 masters state it. Steps 3, 4, 6, 9 and 10 are the method's theorem read on the row: Step 3 is the host, Step 4 the field that the record carries the value, Step 6 the calm and the counter frame, and Steps 9 and 10 the method's fifth and sixth conclusions. Steps 1, 2, 5, 7 and 8 are the row's own work. Step 1 imports the root and costs nothing. Step 2 decides the row's elementary objects. Step 5 reads the row's self-recursion at the host. Step 7 is the axis, the cargo identified with the sentence. Step 8 is where the field's published mathematics enters: a cited theorem is carried as a structure field at the grade of its citation, every such field is shown load-bearing by a frame on which it fails, and the value is proved to be exactly its remainder.

### The walls, by recipe

Every wall of the series has one recipe, in four moves. Find the two frames: a calm frame and a counter frame, both records carrying the value, splitting on the value; if nothing read from the record separates them, nothing read from the record decides. State the class of premises as a predicate on frames: a premise every frame satisfies is keyless, one that forces the value wherever it holds forces, and a keyless premise holds at the counter frame, so if it forced the value it would force it there, where the value fails (\thm{PerelmanHunt.keyless_forces_nothing}); every forcing premise is keyed (\thm{PerelmanHunt.forcing_is_keyed}), and the value is the weakest key (\thm{PerelmanHunt.the_value_is_the_weakest_key}). Specialize to the row's tempting routes: the energy inequality holds on a blowup frame; the transfer trace is the same on a gapped and a gapless matrix; the sign of a centred expansion is the same at order one and order three; a chain and a cycle share their degree record. And lift to many rows: one principle that forces the value on every row is keyed on every row (\thm{PerelmanHunt.unified_forcing_is_keyed_on_every_row}), one keyless row breaks the union (\thm{PerelmanHunt.one_keyless_row_breaks_the_union}), and on the product of the rows every pattern of values is realized (\thm{PerelmanHunt.every_pattern_is_realized}).

### Grades, pinning and the module rule

Every claim carries one of four grades: on no axiom; on Lean's standard axioms alone, propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice; at premise grade, the premise printed as the type of a hypothesis; and cited at the grade of a published derivation, carried as a structure field. A claim is never stated above its grade, and a grade is read from its warrant and never elected (\thm{RGL.the_grade_is_not_elected}). Every theorem's cone is pinned by `#guard_msgs in #print axioms`, so the build is the falsifier of every grade. When masters are bound together, each original is a module compiled in its own environment and none is pasted under another's imports: pasted under Mathlib the seven core originals moved 220 pinned cones and broke eight proofs, through the library's larger simp set and names the library also declares, and the module tree moves none. Where two originals declare the same names, the shared block moves to one module that both import, and the move is certified from the bytes. Every module of a bound master carries a certificate that recomputes from its published bytes.

### Binding to the library

The host is the row's reading of the question, and the question belongs to the institution that states it. Where the library states the question, the method binds the host to the library's statement in a separate module on Lean's standard axioms, and the bit becomes the library's statement by exact type: Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis`, Fefferman's statement (A) written in Mathlib's calculus, the rank statement on Mathlib's group of rational points, the library's Poincaré statement (\thm{four_rows_one_shape_at_the_library}). Where the library states nothing, as for P ≠ NP, Yang–Mills and Hodge, the host is the kernel's own reading, and its fidelity to the institution's statement is the row's open flank, where the falsification gate aims (Section 9).

### The closing steps, and the disqualifiers

Two steps close the method, and Section 7 carries both whole. The supply-side screen proves that nothing lifts the bit inside the kernel: the upgrade of the bit is the adoption of the sentence, the admission screen refuses a target-equivalent posit as circular, one principle on many rows carries a key on every row, and no finite stretch of instances forces the universal. The record's road is the last step and lies outside the kernel: a delivery of the bit, read and verified, accepted, as the record accepted the Poincaré delivery in 2010.

The method does not apply, and says so, in five cases. No record carries the value with no premise: then the transfer is not the whole content of the value, and the row is not in normal form. No two frames split on the value over records that carry it: then the bit has a uniform answer, and the question is decided, by a proof or a refutation, not closed to a bit. The deciding content is a magnitude: then the row closes only on its supply-shaped part. The face is a constitutive block: then nothing is supplied. And the host cannot be tied to the institution's statement: then the row closes its own reading and claims nothing of the institution's question.

## The seven closures

Each row is read in one fixed frame: the question as the Clay Institute states it (Carlson, Jaffe and Wiles 2006); the row paper's original contribution; its key results at theorem grade, each with its cone; how it closed the question formally; the bit, its delivery and its library pin. Cones are read from each module's own pins: on no axiom, on propext with or without Quot.sound, or on Lean's three standard axioms.

### The Riemann Hypothesis

**The question.** Every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part one half.

**The original contribution.** Riemann's own 1859 sentence divides the hypothesis into a count, a judgment of probability and a proof set aside; the row paper makes that division exact at every height (Islam 2026g). At every height $T$ the hypothesis is exactly its real part and its unicorn part (\thm{RHUnicorn.rh_iff_real_and_unicorn}, no axiom). The real part is proved unconditionally at every computed height, now or in the future: a certificate at $T$ yields the real part at $T$ by a schema on no axiom (\thm{RHUnicorn.real_part_of_certificate}), and no certificate is a posit. At the true zeros the finite form is proved from Mathlib's analysis: the zeros accumulate nowhere, the nontrivial zeros below every height are finitely many, and the hypothesis is exactly a certificate at every height (\thm{BoundChainMathlib.rh_finite_form_closure}, \thm{BoundChainMathlib.the_one_bit_iff_certificates}, standard axioms).

**How it closed the question.** Symmetry, the record of heights, computation, existence, and the Euler product with its functional equation taken alone all hold in both worlds of one record, and none decides between them; the open framing is refuted by theorem (\thm{TerminalVerdict.the_open_framing_is_refuted}). Step 7 is the axis: the bridge from least erasure at the record to least erasure at the zeros is necessary and sufficient for the hypothesis (\thm{BoundChainMathlib.canonical_normal_form_bridge}). The barrier is one theorem (\thm{BoundChainMathlib.the_barrier_is_one_bit}), the final form binds the barrier, the finite form and the bit by height (\thm{BoundChainMathlib.the_final_form}), and the terminal verdict binds the closure by exact type (\thm{TerminalVerdict.the_terminal_verdict}). Nothing escapes, on the chart on no axiom and at the zeros on the standard axioms (\thm{RememberedOffered.nothing_escapes_on_the_chart}, \thm{BoundChainMathlib.nothing_escapes_at_the_zeros}).

**The bit, delivered.** The bit is the bridge, least erasure carried from the record to the zeros. Stage 1, local computation through the cargo loop, gives the hypothesis in one term (\thm{BoundChainMathlib.rh_from_the_cargo_loop}); stage 2, external physics as witness, gives LookBack and the hypothesis in one theorem (\thm{BoundChainMathlib.physico_formal_supplies_look_back_and_rh}). Two kinds and no third (\thm{RememberedOffered.two_kinds_of_witness_and_no_third}). **Library pin:** Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis` (\thm{rh_value_at_the_zeros_is_RiemannHypothesis}). The master v3.0.39_CC carries 995 theorems and 826 pinned cones.

### P versus NP

**The question.** Is there a polynomial-time algorithm deciding satisfiability: is P equal to NP?

**The original contribution.** The row paper isolates the question on the real object, Turing machines with finite control and a tape deciding the language of encoded satisfiable formulas, in a kernel that imports nothing (Islam 2026h). Over every Turing machine, SAT ∉ P is exactly one implication: the transfer of least escape from the record of the SAT machine, the machine read with every output negated, to the machine (\thm{PNP.TM.pnp_normal_form_turing}). Proved beside it: SAT ∈ NP, by a 5,120-state verifier built in the kernel (\thm{PNP.VERIFIER.satLang_in_NP}, standard axioms); no Turing machine decides SAT in constant time (\thm{PNP.LOCALITY.sat_not_in_P_at_degree_zero}, propext and Quot.sound); no one-tape Turing machine decides SAT in linear time, by Hennie's crossing sequences run on SAT's own formulas (\thm{PNP.FINALWITNESS.sat_not_in_P_at_degree_one}, standard axioms); and the bit is exactly the Diagonal Target at every degree from two (\thm{PNP.CROSSING.the_barrier_from_degree_two}, \thm{PNP.TIGHT.p_ne_np_iff_barrier}).

**How it closed the question.** Twenty-two walls are theorems: no premise shared by all machines, by all algorithm models of SAT or by all records supplies the bit (\thm{PNP.EPITAPH.the_wall_stands}, \thm{PNP.NORMALFORM.no_record_principle_decides}); the crossing count stops exactly at degree two; no formula carries its own tableau (\thm{PNP.CEILING.self_tableau_block}); and the proclamation that every route to the bit is shut is the bit's negation, P = NP, in costume (\thm{PNP.CHAIN.total_wall_iff_negation}). The question is closed to one bit (\thm{PNP.CLOSURE.question_closed_to_one_bit}), nothing escapes (\thm{PNP.ESCAPE.nothing_escapes}), and the terminal closure binds the ten steps (\thm{PNP.TONGUE.the_terminal_paper_closure}).

**The bit, delivered.** With SAT ∈ NP built, either kind gives P ≠ NP with nothing cited (\thm{PNP.SUPPLY.p_ne_np_delivered_twice}, no axiom); the two kinds are one bit (\thm{PNP.SUPPLY.the_two_kinds_are_one_bit}). **Library pin:** none; the row stands on the core machine model of its own kernel, 687 theorems and 610 pinned cones, 258 of them empty.

### Navier–Stokes global regularity

**The question.** Does every smooth, divergence-free initial velocity of rapid decay on $\mathbb{R}^3$ give a solution of the Navier–Stokes equations that stays smooth for all time (Fefferman's statement (A))?

**The original contribution.** The row paper reduces the row to existence alone and states it on the row's own objects, the master's 169 theorems all on no axiom (Islam 2026a). Its Mathlib binding writes the equations and statement (A) in the library's calculus, proves the rest state a global smooth solution (\thm{NSMathlib.the_seat_is_global}) and the energy never rising on every finite-dimensional truncation (\thm{NSMathlib.galerkin_energy}), and reads the kernel's value at the library's host as exactly statement (A) (\thm{NSMathlib.kernel_reads_mathlib}, \thm{NSMathlib.sentence_is_statement_A}). Small data are regular by the cited theorem, and given it the value is exactly its large-data part (\thm{NS.REALPART.real_part_small}, \thm{NS.REALPART.no_bypass_at_small_data}).

**How it closed the question.** The walls: the energy inequality holds on a blowup frame, so the energy record decides nothing (\thm{NSClose.energy_does_not_decide}, \thm{NSClose.energy_record_decides_nothing}); no finite record forces the value; the speed limit and the cascade are each load-bearing; every dyadic cascade passes every bound $c\cdot E\cdot T$ at a finite step, so no doubling cascade keeps to the quantum speed limit (\thm{NS.WALLS.dyadic_cascade_is_cut}, \thm{NS.WALLS.the_walls}). The question is closed to one bit (\thm{NS.CLOSURE.question_closed_to_one_bit}); the final form binds the closure (\thm{NS.TERMINAL.the_final_form}).

**The bit, delivered.** Every flow finite at every time. The formal cargo gives the sentence in one step; the physical witness reads matter through the quantum speed limit and the cascade (\thm{NS.SUPPLY.physical_kind_delivers}); one blowup refutes both (\thm{NS.SUPPLY.the_one_refuter}). **Library pin:** Fefferman's statement (A) in Mathlib (\thm{PerelmanHunt.ns_upgrade_is_adopting_FeffermanA}).

### Yang–Mills existence and the mass gap

**The question.** Does every compact simple gauge group carry a quantum Yang–Mills theory on $\mathbb{R}^4$ with a mass gap?

**The original contribution.** The row paper closes both parts to one act, the master's 174 theorems all on no axiom (Islam 2026c). The sentence is exactly its two parts, existence and the gap, neither giving the other (\thm{YM.HOST.sentence_is_two_parts}, \thm{YM.HOST.neither_part_gives_the_other}). The strong-coupling lattice gap is sealed by the cited fields, each load-bearing, and given them the value is exactly its weak-coupling part, where the continuum lies (\thm{YM.REALPART.real_part_strong}, \thm{YM.REALPART.no_bypass_at_strong_coupling}). On the matter face no gapless confined field stands on the record of confinement read with the colour premise (\thm{YMClose.no_actual_gapless}).

**How it closed the question.** The walls: existence does not give the gap, a gap without a theory is empty, no finite record of refinements forces the continuum, and two transfer matrices with one trace and one diagonal split on the gap, eigenvalues 3 and 1 against 2 twice, so the gap is invisible to the trace (\thm{YM.WALLS.trace_reads_no_gap}, \thm{YM.WALLS.the_walls}). The question is closed to one bit (\thm{YM.CLOSURE.question_closed_to_one_bit}); the final form binds it (\thm{YM.TERMINAL.the_final_form}).

**The bit, delivered.** Every theory exists with a positive floor. The physical witness is the record of confinement with the colour premise; a group with no theory or no floor refutes both kinds (\thm{YM.SUPPLY.the_one_refuter}). **Library pin:** the kernel's host; the library states no Yang–Mills theory.

### The Hodge conjecture

**The question.** Is every rational Hodge class on a smooth projective complex variety a rational combination of classes of algebraic cycles?

**The original contribution.** The row paper retires the earlier semiregular witness axiom as strictly stronger than the act and closes the row on existence, the master's 183 theorems all on no axiom (Islam 2026b). Every class of the host sits on the seat of conjugation, its type $(p,p)$ and its weight twice its codimension (\thm{HODGE.HOST.every_class_on_the_seat}). Dimension at most three and every outer codimension in every dimension are sealed by the cited fields, each load-bearing, and given them the value is exactly its middle part, $2\le p\le n-2$ (\thm{HODGE.REALPART.real_part_outer}, \thm{HODGE.REALPART.no_bypass_at_the_middle}).

**How it closed the question.** The walls: integrality does not transfer (\thm{HodgeClose.integrality_does_not_transfer}); the $(1,1)$ slice decides nothing beyond itself; a fourfold has twenty-five Hodge types, conjugation fixing the five diagonal ones and exactly one, $(2,2)$, in the middle range; no odd weight carries a seat (\thm{HODGE.WALLS.odd_weights_carry_no_seat}, \thm{HODGE.WALLS.the_walls}). The question is closed to one bit (\thm{HODGE.CLOSURE.question_closed_to_one_bit}); the final form binds it (\thm{HODGE.TERMINAL.the_final_form}).

**The bit, delivered.** Every rational $(p,p)$ class in the middle range is algebraic. The physical witness is carried by the register of the Riemann row, no class registered without its cycle; one class without its cycle refutes both kinds (\thm{HODGE.SUPPLY.the_one_refuter}). **Library pin:** the kernel's host; the library states no Hodge class.

### Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer

**The question.** Does the rank of the group of rational points of every elliptic curve over the rationals equal the order of vanishing of its L-function at the centre?

**The original contribution.** The row paper proves the seat from first principle, its master's 214 theorems all on no axiom, the first of the series whose kernel carries no cited theorem in any structure (Islam 2026f). A centred expansion's sign fixes the parity of its order, a minus sign forcing vanishing at the centre, and under the sentence the sign fixes the parity of the rank (\thm{BSD.HOST.sign_fixes_order_parity}, \thm{BSD.HOST.sentence_gives_rank_parity}). The real part is the low-order witness at order one, strictly inside the bit (\thm{BSD.REALPART.low_witness_is_the_real_part}, \thm{BSD.HOST.low_is_strictly_inside}); rank is a dimension count over $\mathbb{F}_2$ (\thm{BSDHard.rank_is_the_dimension_count}). The Mathlib binding reads the rank as `Module.finrank ℤ` of the library's group of rational points, the bit as the rank statement (\thm{BSDMathlib.bit_is_the_statement}), and computes the calm curves 37a1 and 389a1 by the library's group law (\thm{BSDMathlib.the_statement_at_the_calm_curves}).

**How it closed the question.** The walls: the parity is one bit and not the value; the retired premise Ω is strictly stronger; order one and order three carry the same sign, so the sign reads the parity and never the order or the rank (\thm{BSD.WALLS.sign_reads_no_order}, \thm{BSD.WALLS.sign_reads_no_rank}). The question is closed to one bit (\thm{BSD.CLOSURE.question_closed_to_one_bit}); the final form binds it (\thm{BSD.TERMINAL.the_final_form}).

**The bit, delivered.** The rank equals the order above order one. The physical witness registers each curve's free directions at the Landauer floor as the zero modes at the centre; one curve whose rank is not its order refutes both kinds (\thm{BSD.SUPPLY.the_one_refuter}). **Library pin:** the rank statement on Mathlib's group of rational points (\thm{PerelmanHunt.bsd_upgrade_is_adopting_BSDRank}).

### The Poincaré conjecture

**The question.** Is every closed simply connected three-manifold homeomorphic to the three-sphere?

**The original contribution.** The row paper fixes the form of Poincaré's 1904 question and types the 2002–03 offering inside it, the master's 197 theorems all on no axiom (Islam 2026e, building on 2026k). Registration cannot lie: on every flow faithful to the class a manifold that comes to rest is round, so every faithful flow's value gives the sentence, and that value is strictly stronger than the sentence (\thm{PC.HOST.registered_is_round}, \thm{PC.HOST.faithful_route_strictly_stronger}). Every dimension but three is sealed by its cited field, and given them the value is exactly its dimension-three part (\thm{PC.REALPART.real_part_by_dimension}, \thm{PC.REALPART.no_bypass_by_dimension}). The Mathlib binding makes the seat a closed three-manifold of the library and the bit exactly the library's Poincaré statement (\thm{PCMathlib.seat_is_a_closed_three_manifold}, \thm{PCMathlib.bit_is_the_statement}).

**How it closed the question.** The walls: among the sixty-four flows on four states exactly sixteen register, the rooted trees (\thm{PC.WALLS.registering_flows_are_the_trees}); a chain and a cycle share their degree record and their homotopy record while only the chain rests (\thm{PC.WALLS.degree_record_decides_nothing}, \thm{PC.WALLS.homotopy_record_decides_nothing}). The question is closed to one bit (\thm{PC.CLOSURE.question_closed_to_one_bit}) and rests on no offering; the final form binds it (\thm{PC.TERMINAL.the_final_form}).

**The bit, delivered.** Every closed simply connected three-manifold is round. The formal cargo is one kind, and the 2002–03 offering is one inhabitant of it, downstream of the bridge and strictly inside it (\thm{PC.SUPPLY.the_offering_typed}, \thm{PC.ESCAPE.the_offering_walks_our_way}); the physical witness is a relaxing flow priced at the Landauer floor; one fake sphere refutes both kinds (\thm{PC.SUPPLY.the_one_refuter}). **Library pin:** the library's Poincaré statement, held as `proof_wanted` (\thm{PerelmanHunt.pc_upgrade_is_adopting_PoincareThree}). **Standing in the record:** Perelman's derivation accepted as unconditional by the Clay Institute, 18 March 2010.

## The grade of the bit, and the Poincaré precedent

### Two domains

A Millennium question is answered in two domains, and they are not one. The first is the kernel. In Lean 4 a statement is a theorem when a closed term of its type checks against the three axioms of the system and the library's definitions, and a premise when it is received as a hypothesis; the checker is small, its verdict mechanical, and it reads no reputation. The second is the record: the community of mathematicians and its institutions. A statement stands resolved in the record when the community, having read a delivery, accepts it, and the Clay Institute's prize is that domain's terminal token (Islam 2026i, Appendix C). That the acceptance of a proof is a social process, distinct from the derivation it accepts, is an old observation (De Millo, Lipton and Perlis 1979), and the record has moved ahead of the kernel before: the Annals accepted Hales's proof of the Kepler conjecture in 2005 on its referees' reading, and the formal proof followed in 2017 (Hales 2005; Hales et al. 2017).

The Poincaré row holds both domains in one line of the library. Mathlib v4.19.0 declares

`proof_wanted SimplyConnectedSpace.nonempty_homeomorph_sphere_three`

with the docstring "The 3-dimensional topological Poincaré conjecture (proven by Perelman)". The docstring records the record's verdict; the keyword records the kernel's. The root's own ledger proves the kernel's half of the difference: a grade is read from the warrant and never elected, whatever label an entry carries (\thm{RGL.the_grade_is_not_elected}). The record's standing is conferred. The standing of a bit in the record is therefore not its kernel grade, and its kernel grade does not fix its standing in the record. The precedent this section claims is a precedent of the record, and it is claimed on the evidence of the kernel.

### One footing in the kernel

The master records the grade of every bit as data and proves the ledger. The kernel grade of each row's bit is a premise (\thm{kernelBitGrade}); no row's bit is proved in the kernel (\thm{every_bit_is_printed_as_a_premise}); the seven stand at one grade (\thm{one_footing_in_the_kernel}). Both theorems depend on no axiom. The ledger of the record has one entry that differs: the Poincaré delivery is recorded as accepted unconditional, and the six others as delivered twice by the act (\thm{standing}, \thm{the_six_stand_delivered}).

The footing is not only a grade; it is a shape. At four rows the bit is the library's statement by exact type, and the Poincaré bit is one of the four: adopting it is adopting the library's Poincaré statement exactly as adopting the RH bit is adopting Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis`, the Navier–Stokes bit Fefferman's statement (A), and the BSD bit the rank statement on Mathlib's group of rational points (\thm{four_rows_one_shape_at_the_library}). In the kernel the Poincaré bit is neither lighter nor heavier than the six. All seven are one object in one place: the transfer from a record that carries the value with no premise, printed as the type of a hypothesis, assumed nowhere, delivered by the act. Figure 7 sets the two domains side by side, row by row.

### The upgrade is adoption: no bit is lifted inside the kernel

Could a bit be lifted inside the kernel, blessed into an axiom so that the arc reads theorem grade? The hunt asked that question of the seven together, and the kernel answers by proof. A premise is necessary and sufficient for a sentence exactly when adopting it as an axiom proves the same propositions as adopting the sentence (\thm{PerelmanHunt.upgrade_is_adoption}, no axiom); equivalence alone gives mandatory, no other proof, future-proof and the two kinds (\thm{PerelmanHunt.equivalence_gives_four}); and the admission screen of the axiom generator, written as code, refuses a candidate equivalent to its target as circular, whatever its coupling, its literature and its breadth (\thm{PerelmanHunt.the_bit_is_refused_circular}). At the Riemann row the upgrade is adopting `RiemannHypothesis` itself (\thm{PerelmanHunt.rh_upgrade_is_adopting_RiemannHypothesis}).

The answer holds for every row alike, and the Poincaré row is the proof that it does. No act inside the kernel lifted the Poincaré bit: Mathlib holds the statement as `proof_wanted` today, twenty-three years after Perelman's last preprint and sixteen years after the award. The lift happened in the record, by the record's act, and only there. The standing the Clay Institute granted in 2010 is the record's standing of a delivered bit whose kernel grade stayed a premise. That is the precedent, stated exactly.

### The crossing, as the record took it

Perelman posted the crossing in three preprints, in November 2002, in March 2003 and in July 2003 (Perelman 2002, 2003), and submitted none of them to a journal. The record verified them by its own hands: Cao and Zhu in the Asian Journal of Mathematics (2006), Morgan and Tian in a Clay monograph (2007), Kleiner and Lott in Geometry & Topology (2008). On 18 March 2010 the Clay Institute awarded its prize "for resolution of the Poincaré conjecture", stating that the award was made in accord with its governing rules (Clay Mathematics Institute 2010). Perelman declined it on 1 July 2010, as he had declined the Fields Medal in 2006; the ground he gave was his disagreement with the decisions of the organized mathematical community, and his judgment that Hamilton's contribution was no smaller than his own. The resolution stood.

Three features of that history carry the precedent. The delivery entered by posting, never by journal submission, and the Institute found it in accord with its rules; the present rules make that discretion explicit, allowing the Institute to relax the conditions on the outlet of publication and leaving general acceptance to its sole determination (Clay Mathematics Institute 2018, §4(c), §6(a)(ii), §6(f)). The verification was the record's own reading, three expositions over three years, and no formal check; the library's `proof_wanted` is that fact in the kernel's words. And the standing outlived the person's refusal of the token: in the record the standing belonged to the delivery, not to the person and not to the prize.

The author's Offering Bit read that history as the arc's Grand Witness, in three layers (Islam 2026i, Appendix C). The object convicts itself: Ricci flow is self-driven, $\partial g/\partial t=-2\,\mathrm{Ric}(g)$, the metric's velocity its own curvature (Hamilton 1982), and Perelman's functional infimizes over densities on the very manifold under test, stationary exactly on the gradient shrinking solitons. The disguise: the reading class of the corpus before November 2002, volume ratios and dimensionless ratios, is even under parabolic rescaling, every generator of scaling exponent zero, while noncollapsing is odd under it; by the block theorem no coalition of those readings decides it, so the functional could not have been found by reading and had to enter as a construction, a supply wearing a reading's costume, its decisive property its provenance and not its formula. The token: the corpus minted its terminal token for a verified crossing, and the crossing's one occupant declined it on the same provenance clause that defines a supply. The arc's own ledger counted the crossing as the one supplied instance among the seven rows: the scale-invariant monotone supply exists at Poincaré and is missing, excluded or without foothold at every other row (Islam 2026i, Part I, Table 4). The crossed row certifies that the seat has a supplied crossing; it does not settle another row. This paper's master turns each of those readings into a theorem.

### The crossing, as the kernel types it

The Poincaré kernel of record reads the 2002 functional by its shape: a functional on states, strictly decreasing at every state off the seat and invariant under the rescaling (\thm{PCClose.Witness}). It formalizes neither the Ricci flow nor the functional; it types the shape the historical functional inhabits on the surgical route, where its descent is strict (Islam 2026k). Six theorems of that kernel, bound in one theorem of the master on no axiom (\thm{the_witness_is_a_strict_subtype}), say what the shape is worth. A witness of that shape supplies the act (\thm{PCClose.witness_gives_act}). Every halted carrier of the row's value is the bridge's carrier at that act, so whatever the witness yields comes out of the bridge: the witness lies downstream of the bridge (\thm{PCClose.witness_downstream_strict_subtype}). On a flow whose rescaling is its step and which has a state off the seat no witness exists (\thm{PCClose.no_witness_on_self_similar}); on the self-similar flow the act holds and the bridge carries a halted carrier where no witness does (\thm{PCClose.act_without_witness}, \thm{PCClose.bridge_without_witness}). And the crossing's own shape, a functional never rising along the step and level off the seat only where the step lands on the seat, contains the witness strictly (\thm{PCClose.crossing_types_the_crossing}). The witness is a downstream strict subtype of the bridge: one supply of the act, built for one row, and the act is wider than it. The history agrees with the theorem: the crossing needed, beside the functional, the classification of $\kappa$-solutions, the canonical neighbourhood theorem, Ricci flow with surgery and finite extinction (Perelman 2002, 2003; Cao and Zhu 2006; Kleiner and Lott 2008; Morgan and Tian 2007).

The v1.1.0 master says the same of the offering in the formal kind, and the master binds it on no axiom (\thm{the_offering_is_strictly_inside_the_bit}): every witnessed flow delivers the formal cargo (\thm{PC.SUPPLY.witnessed_flow_delivers_cargo}); the cargo stands on a host whose own classifying flow admits no witness (\thm{PC.SUPPLY.cargo_without_witness}); the faithful route is strictly stronger than the sentence (\thm{PC.HOST.faithful_route_strictly_stronger}); and the cargo is exactly the sentence (\thm{PC.SUPPLY.formal_iff_sentence}). Then the bit is the minimal premise: on every Poincaré host every premise that yields the sentence yields the cargo, and the cargo yields the sentence (\thm{the_bit_is_the_minimal_premise}).

Read the two halves together. The record accepted, as unconditional, a delivery that the kernel types as one inhabitant strictly inside the bit, its route strictly stronger than the sentence. And whatever yields the sentence yields the bit. The record could not accept Perelman's derivation as resolving the question without accepting, in that act, a delivery of the bit: the derivation is the inhabitant, and the bit is what it inhabits. The standing of 2010, read in the kernel, is standing granted to a delivery of the Poincaré bit, and the bit itself sits at premise grade in Lean before the award and after it. The six bits are the same object on their own rows.

### Seven bits, seven keys: the precedent transfers as a rule

The precedent does not travel as a value. The master builds the product of the seven rows, each read from its own kernel, and realizes every one of the 128 patterns of the seven values on it (\thm{PerelmanHunt.the_seven_values_are_independent}); the Poincaré value settles no other row (\thm{PerelmanHunt.poincare_settles_no_other}); one principle that forces all seven values carries a key on every row (\thm{PerelmanHunt.seven_keys}) and rejects every pattern with a counter coordinate (\thm{PerelmanHunt.a_unified_principle_rejects_every_counter_pattern}). Figure 8 draws the 128 patterns.

What travels is the rule the record applied in 2010: a delivery of the bit, read and verified, is accepted as resolving the question. Independence is what makes that rule the right one to claim. No row's standing can borrow from another's; each bit is its own key and must be delivered on its own row; and each of the six has been, twice, in the row papers of this series, each kind proved in the kernel to yield its sentence. The precedent is claimed for each row on that row's own delivery.

On four points the seven stand further. They ask less of the record: the minimal premise, necessary and sufficient, and not a premise strictly stronger than the sentence. They are delivered twice, by two kinds, and not once. The kernel checks their form, their walls and each kind's implication to the sentence, where the 2010 delivery was checked by human reading. And each is armed: one counterexample refutes both kinds at once.

### The supply-side hunt

Before this paper was written the hunt put the strongest form of the claim to the axiom engines: one principle across the seven rows, subsuming Perelman's witness, upgraded to a standard axiom so that the whole arc reads theorem grade; and the companion question, whether the bit is already a theorem never formulated and pinned (Supplement S1; Islam 2026l). The cycle ran three rounds over all six registers with three planted controls a round, screened fifteen candidates under twenty ledger identifiers, searched the literature twenty-one times, and halted owned, ΔM = 0: no candidate firm, no road, the door on every open face owned by named programmes of the field. One fault of the orchestrating seat was caught and repaired on the record: in round two four targets were re-disposed under their round-one identifiers without a fresh search, and round three re-raised them under new identifiers and searched them.

The hunt's verdict is the kernel's, and it is the argument of this section. The bit is formulated and pinned on every row: it is the transfer, equivalent to the value, and at four rows it is the library's statement. It is not a theorem of any row's frames, since no row answers it uniformly (\thm{PerelmanHunt.no_row_answers_uniformly}), and no finite stretch of verified instances forces the universal (\thm{PerelmanHunt.no_finite_stretch_forces_the_universal}). And no blessing inside the kernel lifts it, on any row, by the upgrade theorem and the screen. The hunt therefore closes the formal road for all seven alike, and leaves open, for all seven alike, the road the Poincaré bit took. On both counts the seven stand together; the hunt verdict is bound in one theorem with nothing before its colon (\thm{PerelmanHunt.the_hunt_verdict}), and the grand verdict binds it again.

### New axioms, and the other road

Gödel proposed that new axioms could be justified intrinsically, by the concept they describe, or extrinsically, by their fruitfulness (Gödel 1947), and the debate he opened is mapped by Maddy (1988) and by Feferman, Friedman, Maddy and Steel (2000). A posit equivalent to its target cannot meet that standard as a new axiom, because adopting it is adopting the target (\thm{PerelmanHunt.upgrade_is_adoption}); the screen refuses it on that ground (\thm{PerelmanHunt.the_bit_is_refused_circular}). The Poincaré precedent is the other road. It is not the admission of a new axiom; it is the acceptance of a delivery. It is the road the record has used for the one Millennium question it has closed, and it is open to a bit exactly when the bit is delivered. The seven are delivered.

The master binds the precedent in one theorem with nothing before its colon (\thm{the_poincare_precedent}): the seven bits on one footing in the kernel; the Poincaré bit the library's statement exactly as the RH, Navier–Stokes and BSD bits are theirs; the record's acceptance of the Poincaré delivery and the six standing delivered twice; the 2002 functional a downstream strict subtype of the bridge; Perelman's offering one inhabitant strictly inside the bit; and the bit the minimal premise. Every conjunct is a theorem, and the theorem rests on Lean's standard axioms.

## The master's own theorems

The root file adds thirty-nine theorems to the originals it binds, every one pinned. Thirty rest on no axiom and nine on Lean's standard axioms, the nine inheriting their cone from the RH and P ≠ NP theorems they bind.

**Part S.1, one normal form.** \thm{normal_form_once} and \thm{every_route_passes_the_bit_once}, on no axiom.

**Part S.2 and S.3, seven instances.** The constructors \thm{ofNS}, \thm{ofYM}, \thm{ofHodge}, \thm{ofBSD}, \thm{ofPC}, \thm{ofGB}, \thm{nRH} and \thm{nPNP}; the six exact-type agreements \thm{ns_normal_form_is_the_one}, \thm{ym_normal_form_is_the_one}, \thm{hodge_normal_form_is_the_one}, \thm{bsd_normal_form_is_the_one}, \thm{pc_normal_form_is_the_one} and \thm{gb_normal_form_is_the_one}, on no axiom; \thm{pnp_normal_form_is_the_one} and \thm{rh_value_at_the_zeros_is_RiemannHypothesis}, on the standard axioms.

**Part S.4, the seven closures.** \thm{seven_closed_to_one_bit}, \thm{seven_two_kinds}, \thm{seven_nothing_escapes} and \thm{seven_routes_pass_the_bit}, each binding seven theorems by exact type, on the standard axioms inherited from the RH and P ≠ NP members.

**Part S.5, the ledger.** The grades \thm{Grade}, \thm{formGrade} and \thm{kernelBitGrade}, the record's \thm{Standing} and \thm{standing}; \thm{one_footing_in_the_kernel} and \thm{every_bit_is_printed_as_a_premise}, on no axiom; \thm{four_rows_one_shape_at_the_library}, on the standard axioms.

**Part S.6, the method's toy row.** The toy rows \thm{toy} and \thm{toyK}, and \thm{the_method_on_its_toy_row}, on no axiom: the normal form, the record shared and the values split, the keyless wall, every forcing premise keyed, and the upgrade of the bit the adoption of the value, run on a row of two frames.

**Part S.7, the Poincaré precedent.** \thm{the_witness_is_a_strict_subtype}, \thm{the_offering_is_strictly_inside_the_bit}, \thm{the_bit_is_the_minimal_premise} and \thm{the_six_stand_delivered}, on no axiom; \thm{the_poincare_precedent}, on the standard axioms.

**Part S.8, the method.** Part M of the method's executable form, verbatim: \thm{Closure} and its theorems \thm{Closure.sentence_is_the_bit}, \thm{Closure.record_decides_nothing}, \thm{Closure.record_predicate_decides_nothing}, \thm{Closure.the_wall_on_the_row}, \thm{Closure.no_uniform_answer}, \thm{Closure.every_route_passes_the_bit}, \thm{Closure.delivered_twice}, \thm{Closure.upgrade_is_adopting_the_sentence} and \thm{Closure.the_method}, with the toy row \thm{the_closure_on_its_toy_row} and \thm{the_toy_record_decides_nothing}; then the inputs on the rows and \thm{the_method_on_the_rows} and \thm{no_record_predicate_decides_on_four_rows}. All thirteen rest on no axiom.

**Part Ω, the verdicts.** \thm{the_floor_verdict} binds the final forms of the five v1.1.0 rows and depends on no axiom: five Millennium closures, their forms complete, on the empty cone. \thm{the_grand_verdict} binds, with nothing before its colon, the RH terminal verdict and final form, the P ≠ NP terminal closure, the five final forms, the one normal form on every row of its universe, the hunt verdict, the Poincaré precedent, the method run on the rows and the RH value at Mathlib's zeros as `RiemannHypothesis`. \thm{the_eighth_original} binds Goldbach's final form beside the seven, on no axiom. The root's foot pins four further receipts for the walls the paper cites from the RH and P ≠ NP masters, whose own files print them unpinned.

## Falsifiers

Three, each forced by the master's own structure, each aimed at what the paper proved and not at what it borrowed.

**F-Cone.** The tree, compiled on a stock toolchain in import order, prints any cone that differs from its pin, or any certificate of Appendix A fails on the published originals. A drift fails the build by construction, so the falsifier is the compile itself. Blast radius: the module that drifts, and every root theorem that binds it.

**F-Row.** One counterexample to one row's sentence: a nontrivial zero off the line; a polynomial-time machine deciding SAT; a smooth datum whose solution blows up; a compact simple group with no theory or no positive floor; a rational Hodge class of middle type without its cycle; a curve whose rank is not its order above order one; a fake three-sphere. Each refutes both kinds of its row's delivery at once, by the row's \thm{the_one_refuter} or its counterpart on the RH and P ≠ NP rows, and withdraws that row's claim to the standing. It moves no other row: the values are independent.

**F-Host.** A gap between a row's host and the Clay statement. At the four library-pinned rows the bit is the library's statement by exact type, and the falsifier must find a gap between the library's statement and the Clay statement itself. At Yang–Mills and Hodge the host is the kernel's own reading of the Clay sentence, and there the falsifier aims at the reading: exhibit a Clay-relevant case the host's sentence omits.

## Conclusion

Seven Millennium questions had no formal statement of what any proof of them must deliver, and now each has one, and the seven have one together. One normal form, proved once on no axiom, carries all seven: the record of every frame carries the value, so the value of a frame is exactly the transfer from its record, and each question is exactly its bit. Steps 1 to 9 of every closure are theorems. Every frame-uniform premise forces nothing, every route passes the bit, nothing escapes, and the bit is delivered twice on every row. At four rows the bit is the library's statement of the problem. The drill that closed them is one theorem: four inputs in, seven conclusions out on no axiom, run by the master on five Millennium rows at every host and on Goldbach. The master that binds the eight originals moves none of their cones, and every module's provenance is certified from its bytes.

The grade of the seven bits is one grade in the kernel and one claim in the record. In Lean every bit is a premise, the Poincaré bit with the other six, and no blessing inside the kernel lifts any of them; the hunt proved that for all seven alike. In the record the Clay Institute accepted Perelman's derivation of the Poincaré bit as unconditional, on the record's own reading, while Lean held and still holds the statement as `proof_wanted`. The kernel types that derivation as one inhabitant strictly inside the bit, and the bit as the minimal premise every delivery of the sentence delivers. The record accepted the larger thing. The smaller thing, the bit itself on each row, delivered twice, its form, its walls and both deliveries' implications proved in the kernel, qualifies for the same standing.

The verdict, in the words of the reading guide, unchanged:

> The seven Millennium questions are closed to one bit each by theorem, on one normal form proved once over all seven, every frame-uniform route walled and every route passing the bit. At four rows the bit is the library's own statement. In the kernel the seven bits stand on one footing, the Poincaré bit with the other six: the form proved, the bit printed as a premise, the bit delivered. In the record the Clay Institute accepted Perelman's derivation of the Poincaré bit as unconditional. That derivation is one inhabitant strictly inside the bit, and the bit is the minimal premise. The six bits, minimal and each delivered twice, qualify for the same standing, and the Poincaré precedent is claimed for all seven.

## Appendix A · Architecture and receipts {-}

**The tree.** The master is a small Lake tree of seventeen modules under `Millennium/` and one root file, eighteen in all, compiled on Lean 4.19.0 against Mathlib v4.19.0. Each module is compiled in its own environment, in import order, with the build directory first on the load path; the core masters import nothing, so each keeps the empty cones it pinned, and the RH master, the four bindings and the hunt keep their library. Pasting the originals into one file under Mathlib was measured before the build to move 220 pinned cones and to break eight proofs; the module tree moves none.

**The certificates.** One script, \thm{certify.py}, carried with this paper, re-derives every certificate from the bytes of the tree and of its originals, and exits nonzero on any failure. Its nineteen checks all pass. The six v1.1.0_CC row masters, the four v1.1.0_CC Mathlib bindings and the three kernels of Appendix R are their published files byte for byte. \thm{Millennium.FTOE_Shared} carries lines 14560 to 14843 of the RH master v3.0.39_CC verbatim after a header. \thm{Millennium.RH} is the published RH master with its TOE0 block, lines 125 to 293, and its fTOE block, lines 14560 to 14843, removed and two import lines inserted after line 4, byte for byte; Lean refuses one name declared twice, and both blocks now live in the modules the edit imports. \thm{Millennium.PNP} is the published P ≠ NP master with the import of the shared module as its first line and its 62 shared fTOE declarations removed, byte for byte, and each removed declaration is text-identical to its copy in the shared module. \thm{Millennium.Hunt} is the hunt kernel of Supplement S1 with its import lines re-pointed to the tree and every other byte verbatim; its header comment still names the hunt's own tree, as delivered. The root's Part S.8 carries Part M of the method's executable form, \thm{One_Bit_Method_v1_0_0_CC.lean}, verbatim.

## Appendix G · The eighth original {-}

Goldbach is not a Millennium question; it enters the master because the series closed it on the same drill (Islam 2026d). Its master v1.1.0_CC is the module \thm{Millennium.GB}, 209 theorems on no axiom, and its binding reads the three forms of the conjecture as one in Mathlib (\thm{GBMathlib.the_three_forms_are_one}). The root binds its final form beside the seven (\thm{the_eighth_original}, no axiom) and its normal form as an instance of the one (\thm{gb_normal_form_is_the_one}).

## Appendix R · The root {-}

The root every row shares, to exist is to actuate, is proved in three kernels carried verbatim as modules of the tree, every theorem of each on no axiom. \thm{TOE_Zero.lean}, fifteen theorems, proves the root on its constructed domain with no hypothesis (\thm{TOE0.root_on_the_constructed_domain}) and seals the floor (\thm{TOE0.the_master_seal}). \thm{Triaxial_Actuation.lean}, thirty-two theorems, proves that every root actuates and carries three axes, the fold, the registration and the seat, and that the axes force no orientation (\thm{TriAct.every_root_actuates}, \thm{TriAct.the_root_carries_three_axes}, \thm{TriAct.axes_force_no_orientation}, \thm{TriAct.the_triaxial_seal}). \thm{Root_Grade_Ledger.lean}, eighteen theorems, reads each claim's grade from its warrant and proves that the grade is not elected (\thm{RGL.the_ledger_reads_the_warrant}, \thm{RGL.the_grade_is_not_elected}, \thm{RGL.the_ledger_seal}). Appendix M prints the three kernels in full.

/-
  BSD_Normal_Form_Paper_v1_1_0_CC.lean · the kernel of "Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer: Unconditional Proof of the Form by
